info.title: VMS camera API
info.description: Camera registration, version-checked display-name updates and logical source/device deletion, lookup and listing, plus legacy contract validation. Registry APIs require explicit database configuration, schema version 7 and the documented runtime grants. Device deletion requires no undeleted child sources. Both deletions use the explicitly reviewed registry-only release with no managed usage creators. Source sessions, ONVIF/PTZ, media ingest and recording are not implemented. Operational activation is a separate step.

get.description: When CAMERA_DATABASE_URL is configured, checks camera migration history and required registry permissions. Otherwise checks HTTP foundation only. business_runtime_ready remains false.

post.description: Validates submitted data only. No resource is persisted, device contacted, reference resolved, or inference run. Maximum body: 65536 bytes.

200.description: Contract valid; resource_created, references_verified and runtime_verified are false

400.description: Malformed JSON, unknown field, trailing value, or wrong field type

post.description: Creates metadata only. Successful responses are retained atomically under a stable authenticated principal, method, path and Idempotency-Key. Same canonical object replays HTTP 201, Location and device fields; different input returns 409. Object key order does not matter; string values are preserved. Each HTTP request has a fresh request_id. Duplicate JSON keys, unknown or incorrectly cased properties, and non-string field values are rejected. Keys have no automatic expiry.

503.description: Registry disabled, unavailable or request could not be confirmed; retry creation with the same key.

get.description: Active devices ordered by ASCII device_id. Unknown/repeated/empty query parameters are invalid. Pagination is not a snapshot; concurrent inserts can affect later pages. No filters in this version. Deleted devices are excluded and a cursor naming a deleted ID continues after that ID.

get.description: New reads exclude deleted devices; historical POST/PATCH response replay never restores a deleted registration.

patch.description: Replaces only display_name. Requires a single Idempotency-Key. Validation order: authentication, method, query, path ID, conditional headers, idempotency key, media/JSON, semantic fields, then storage. Successful replay precedes current-state/version checks. Each new successful command increments version, including an unchanged name; replay does not. created_at and child sources/profiles stay unchanged; updated_at never decreases. Success is stored atomically with the update under the stable authenticated principal, PATCH, canonical device path and key. Equivalent JSON key order/escapes replay; other values conflict. Keys have no automatic expiry. Body limit is 64 KiB. The development shared principal is not production IAM.

200.description: Updated device or historical first-success snapshot, even after later changes; a fresh request_id is returned on every HTTP request.

400.description: QUERY_INVALID, PRECONDITION_HEADER_UNSUPPORTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID or INVALID_JSON. No query or If-Match/If-None-Match/If-Unmodified-Since header is accepted.

409.description: DEVICE_VERSION_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT or DEVICE_VERSION_EXHAUSTED. Read the current device before a new version-conditioned command.

422.description: CONTRACT_INVALID: missing fields, invalid schema version/path ID, nonpositive expected_version or invalid display name.

503.description: REGISTRY_DISABLED or DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE. If the result is uncertain, retry with the same key and body.

delete.description: Logically deletes one device registration using expected_version. The same device advisory lock as CreateSource precedes the active device row lock, exact version/exhaustion check, a separate undeleted-child check and trusted managed-usage guard. READ COMMITTED sees preceding source commits after the lock. Any undeleted child yields DEVICE_HAS_ACTIVE_SOURCES even without live media use. All children must first be individually deleted using Source DELETE; there is no force/cascade/purge/restore or implicit cleanup. Device tombstone, version+1, deleted_at=updated_at (UTC, never before prior updated_at) and the durable receipt commit atomically. Device ID/kind/name/created_at, deleted children/profiles and all POST/PATCH/DELETE histories remain unchanged. Deleted IDs/channels remain reserved. Authentication, method, query (including a bare question mark), decoded path, conditional headers, key, media/JSON and semantics precede storage. Successful principal/DELETE/canonical path/key receipts replay before current state/version/children/usage checks, including after restart/token rotation; changed valid bodies with a successful key conflict. Keys have no automatic expiry; failures record nothing and can be retried with the same body/key. New GET/PATCH/DELETE hide the deleted device, new lists exclude it, and cursors continue after its ID. Old device/source successes replay without resurrection. New source creation after parent deletion returns DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE with no persisted source/profile/receipt. A reviewed server-side registry-only profile, shared with source deletion, confirms absence of managed device/session/consumer/adapter creators; unknown policy/usage fails closed. Future usage admission must share the device advisory and row locks. Unlike sources, lowercase validate (including URL escapes) is a valid device ID. Limit 64 KiB and exact int64 JSON integer token. The stable shared development principal is not production IAM.

200.description: First deletion receipt or identical durable receipt on replay; 200 in both cases. DELETED and runtime_verified=false, fresh request_id matching X-Request-ID, Idempotency-Replayed false/true, no Location, Cache-Control no-store. No device snapshot, child list, profiles or credentials are returned.

400.description: QUERY_INVALID, PRECONDITION_HEADER_UNSUPPORTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID or INVALID_JSON. No query or If-Match/If-None-Match/If-Unmodified-Since header is accepted.

404.description: DEVICE_NOT_FOUND: no active device exists for a new command.

409.description: DEVICE_VERSION_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, DEVICE_VERSION_EXHAUSTED, DEVICE_HAS_ACTIVE_SOURCES or DEVICE_IN_USE. A failed command writes no tombstone or success record. Version conflict precedes active children.

422.description: CONTRACT_INVALID: missing fields, schema_version other than v1, invalid decoded device ID or nonpositive expected_version.

503.description: REGISTRY_DISABLED, DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE or DEVICE_USAGE_UNAVAILABLE. Unknown usage/profile denies deletion; database/receipt failure rolls back changes. Retry an uncertain result with the same key/body.

Same canonical object replays HTTP 201, Location and source fields; different input returns 409. Object key order does not matter; string values are preserved. Each HTTP request has a fresh request_id. Duplicate JSON keys, unknown or incorrectly cased properties, and non-string field values are rejected. Keys have no automatic expiry.

409.description: SOURCE_EXISTS, SOURCE_CHANNEL_EXISTS, DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE or IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Failed requests do not consume their key.

get.description: Active sources ordered by ASCII source_id, including profiles in registration order. Optional exact device_id filter; an unknown device returns an empty page. Cursors belong to the source collection and the exact filter (including no filter); retain device_id on subsequent pages, while limit may change. Unknown/repeated/empty query parameters and invalid or mismatched cursors return 400 QUERY_INVALID. Pagination is not a snapshot across requests: new IDs after the cursor may appear, and earlier new IDs require restarting the listing. Each page reads source metadata and profiles in one SQL snapshot. Items are registration metadata, not live stream status.

patch.description: Replaces only source display_name using the source expected_version, independently of the parent device version. Preserves identifiers, parent, channel, transport/input/motion modes, profile values/order, primary profile and created_at. Validation order: authentication, method, query, path ID, conditional headers, idempotency key, media/JSON, semantic fields, then storage. Successful replay precedes current-state/version checks. Each new command increments version even for the same name; updated_at never decreases. The full source snapshot including profiles is committed atomically with the update, scoped to the stable principal, PATCH, canonical source path and key. Equivalent key order/string escapes replay; different values conflict. POST and device PATCH keys are independent. Keys have no automatic expiry. Limit 64 KiB. Exact source_id validate and equivalent URL escapes are reserved: PATCH returns 405/Allow: POST. The shared development principal is not production IAM.

200.description: Updated source with ordered profiles, or the historical first-success snapshot even after later changes. Returns a fresh request_id, registration_state REGISTERED and runtime_verified false. No Location header.

400.description: QUERY_INVALID, PRECONDITION_HEADER_UNSUPPORTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID or INVALID_JSON. No query or If-Match/If-None-Match/If-Unmodified-Since header is accepted.

503.description: REGISTRY_DISABLED or DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE. If the result is uncertain, retry with the same key and body.

delete.description: Logically deletes one source registration using expected_version. Preserves the source ID/channel reservation, profiles and successful POST/PATCH/DELETE history; does not delete the parent or sibling sources. No physical deletion or media cleanup. First success increments version once and commits deleted_at=updated_at (UTC, never earlier than the previous updated_at) with the receipt in one transaction. Authentication, method, query, decoded path, conditional headers, key, media/JSON and semantic validation precede storage. No query is accepted, including a bare question mark. The durable principal/DELETE/canonical path/key scope is independent of POST and PATCH. Matching successful requests replay before current state/version/usage checks, including after deletion or process/token rotation; a changed body with that key conflicts. Keys have no automatic expiry. A new request after deletion returns 404; GET and new lists exclude deleted rows. Old POST/PATCH successes replay historical snapshots without resurrection. This release uses an explicitly reviewed server-side registry-only policy with no session/consumer/adapter creators. Unknown policy/usage fails closed; future runtime admission must share the source row transaction. Limit 64 KiB. Exact lowercase validate (including URL escapes) is reserved: DELETE returns 405/Allow: POST. The shared development principal is not production IAM.

200.description: First deletion receipt or the identical durable receipt on replay; 200 in both cases. DELETED and runtime_verified=false, fresh request_id matching X-Request-ID, Idempotency-Replayed false/true, no Location, Cache-Control no-store. No source snapshot or profiles are returned.

400.description: QUERY_INVALID, PRECONDITION_HEADER_UNSUPPORTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID or INVALID_JSON. No query or If-Match/If-None-Match/If-Unmodified-Since header is accepted.

409.description: SOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, SOURCE_VERSION_EXHAUSTED or SOURCE_IN_USE. A failed command writes no deletion or success record.

503.description: REGISTRY_DISABLED, DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE or SOURCE_USAGE_UNAVAILABLE. Unknown usage/policy denies deletion; database/receipt failure rolls back all changes. Retry an uncertain result using the same key and body.
